To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of secondary education and the quantity of secondary education have a positive effect on earnings, that these effects are large enough to account for a significant part of the difference in earnings between Kenya and Tanzania, and that the effect of secondary education on earnings is large enough to account, in part, for a large part of the difference between the labor productivity of Kenya and Tanzania.

(1) the Kenyan secondary school system is more efficient and effective than that in Tanzania; (2) Kenyan students are better prepared to enter the labor market; (3) Kenyan workers earn higher wages than their Tanzanian counterparts, and (4) the difference in earnings between the two countries can largely be attributed to the different educational policies followed in each country.

(a) the effect of schooling on earnings is substantial, (b) the quality of schooling is important for the effect of schooling, (c) the quality of secondary schooling is more important for the earnings effect of schooling than is the quality of primary schooling, (d) the effect of secondary schooling is larger than the effect of primary schooling, and (e) the effect of education is larger in Kenya than in Tanzania.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of education on productivity and earnings.
the effects of education on productivity.
the effect of education and other factors on the earnings of Kenyan workers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

education is a very important factor in the determination of productivity and that the productivity gains to be expected in Kenya from a policy change to a more generous secondary education system are very substantial indeed.
education in the form of schooling has a significant effect on earnings, but that this is not necessarily a measure of its productivity.
the Kenyan education system is superior to the Tanzanian system in terms of its impact on the productivity of labor and the earnings of individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
education is an investment that yields substantial returns to individuals and to society.
education has a large and positive effect on productivity.
the Kenyan education policy is more effective than the Tanzanian one, but the Tanzanian policy is more efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the quality of education is important, the quantity of education is even more important.
the effect of education policy on economic development can be measured with reasonable accuracy, and that the results are important.
the quality and quantity of education have a significant impact on earnings and productivity, which is consistent with a large literature on the returns to education.
